lenses.sp: Wants a large, steady, cheap company with a strong balance sheet.
lenses.vd: In Benjamin Graham's spirit: would probably pass (2 checks use fewer years than the rule needs).

ch.r: Market value above ₹5,000 crore
ch.w: Graham avoided small companies; ₹5,000 crore is our Indian translation of 'adequate size'.

ch.r: Current assets ÷ current liabilities ≥ 2
ch.w: For every ₹100 it owes within a year, it holds ₹343 of cash, stock and dues coming in.

ch.r: Long-term debt ≤ current assets − current liabilities
ch.v: Long-term debt ₹66 cr vs working capital ₹668 cr
ch.w: Graham wanted the short-term cushion alone to be able to repay long-term loans.

ch.n: A profit every year for 10 years
ch.r: Positive earnings in each of the last 10 years
ch.v: Profit in all 4 yrs we have
ch.w: No loss in the years we can see; the earlier years are not in the free data.

ch.r: Dividends every year for 20 years (India: 10 years)
ch.w: NSE corporate actions not fetched.

ch.n: Earnings per share up a third in 10 years
ch.r: EPS +33% over 10 years (3-year averages at each end)
ch.w: EPS (average of the first 2 vs last 2 years we have) moved +5%.

ch.r: PE ≤ 15 on 3-year average earnings
ch.w: You pay ₹18 for every ₹1 of average yearly profit over the last 3 yrs.
You pay ₹2.65 for every ₹1 of net worth.

ch.r: Price < √(22.5 × EPS × book value per share)
ch.w: With EPS ₹24.7 and book value ₹164 per share, Graham's ceiling price is ₹302.

lenses.st: Wonderful business at a fair price
lenses.sp: Wants a simple business with a lasting edge, high returns without debt, and trustworthy managers.
lenses.vd: In Warren Buffett's spirit: a great business, and the price passes both this lens's own price test and the fair-value check (₹435 vs fair value ₹498).

ch.r: Could you explain how it makes money in two sentences?
q: What does it sell, and to whom?
Will people still need this in 10 years?

ch.r: A lasting edge: brand, low cost, network or switching costs
q: Why can't a well-funded rival copy it?
Has it kept high returns through bad years?

ch.r: ROE ≥ 15% in at least 8 of the last 10 years, with debt-to-equity < 0.5
ch.w: Strong in 4 of the 4 yrs we can see.

ch.r: No loss in 10 years
ch.w: No loss in the years we can see.

ch.n: Doesn't eat its cash in capex
ch.r: Capex < 50% of operating cash flow (5-year sum)
ch.v: Capex was 34% of cash from operations over 4 yrs
ch.w: Of every ₹100 of cash the business brought in, ₹34 went back into plant and equipment.

ch.r: Share count up no more than 5% over the years we have
ch.w: Your slice of the company hasn't been shrunk by new share issues.

ch.r: Candid, sensible with capital, no governance red flags
ch.v: No management red flags in our automatic checks (checked: credit ratings, pledge).
ch.w: Our automatic checks are a starting point only.
q: Do they admit mistakes in the annual report letter?
Have past acquisitions and capex paid off?

ch.n: Bought with a margin of safety
ch.r: Price ≥ 25% below estimated intrinsic value
ch.w: Needs the fair-value (DCF) estimate, which arrives in Stage 4.

lenses.st: Great business at a fair price; invert
lenses.sp: Prefers a great business at a fair price, and first asks how the investment could fail.
lenses.vd: In Charlie Munger's spirit: would see a mixed picture (1 checks use fewer years than the rule needs).

ch.r: Average ROCE ≥ 20% over 5 years
ch.w: For every ₹100 in the business it earned about ₹25 a year.

ch.r: PEG (PE ÷ EPS growth) below 2
ch.w: PE 17.6 against EPS growth of 6.0% a year.

ch.r: Promoters own ≥ 25%, none pledged
ch.w: Shareholding not fetched.

ch.n: Invert: how could this go wrong?
ch.r: List the ways you could lose money before the reasons to buy
ch.v: Starter list from our checks: Thinly traded – hard to buy or sell without moving the price
q: What would make profits halve?
What would a short-seller say?

ch.r: Only invest in what you truly understand
q: Could you explain this business to a 12-year-old in 2 minutes?

lenses.st: Growth at a reasonable price · type: Slow grower
lenses.sp: First sorts the company by type (this one looks like a slow grower), then wants growth at a sensible PEG with low debt.
lenses.vd: In Peter Lynch's spirit: a great business, but this lens's own price test fails.

ch.r: PEG < 1 attractive, ~1 fair, ≥ 2 expensive
ch.w: PE 17.6 divided by EPS growth 6.0% a year (growth measured over 3 yrs).

ch.r: Debt-to-equity below 0.35
ch.w: ₹5 borrowed for every ₹100 of shareholders' money.

ch.r: EPS growth 20–25% a year
ch.w: Only for fast growers; this looks like a slow grower.

ch.r: Inventory should not grow faster than sales
ch.w: Unsold goods rising faster than sales can mean demand is weakening.

ch.r: Insider buying is a green flag
ch.w: No insider trades disclosed to NSE in the last 12 months.

ch.r: A buyback is a green flag
ch.w: No buyback in the last 3 years (not a negative).

ch.n: Not a hot stock in a hot industry
ch.r: Avoid what everyone is excited about
q: Is this stock being talked about everywhere?
Has it more than doubled in a year on hopes rather than profits?

lenses.st: Outstanding growth companies, held for years
lenses.sp: Pays up for long growth runways, rising margins and candid, capable managers.
lenses.vd: In Philip Fisher's spirit: would likely find a lot to like (2 checks use fewer years than the rule needs).

ch.r: Sales growth ≥ 10% a year for many years
ch.w: Fisher wanted products with room for years of sales growth.

ch.r: Steady R&D and new products
ch.w: R&D spending isn't in the free data; check the annual report (pharma: R&D 6–10% of sales).

ch.r: Profit margin in the top 40% of its sector
ch.w: Fisher looked for companies earning more on each rupee of sales than rivals.

ch.r: Operating margin flat or rising over the years
ch.w: Fisher wanted managers working to lift margins.

ch.r: Share count up no more than 5% over the years we have
ch.w: Your slice of the company hasn't been shrunk by new share issues.

ch.r: Low staff turnover, no long strikes
q: Any strikes or high attrition mentioned in the annual report?

ch.r: Management talks openly about problems
q: In a bad quarter, did the concall explain why, or only blame the market?

ch.r: Ask customers, suppliers and competitors
q: What do people who use or sell its products say?

lenses.sp: Ranks every company on 'cheap' and 'good' and buys the best combined ranks.
lenses.vd: In Joel Greenblatt's spirit: would see a mixed picture.

ch.r: Earnings yield (EBIT ÷ EV) in the top 30%
ch.w: The business earns ₹9.5 of operating profit a year for every ₹100 you'd pay for all of it (shares + debt − cash).

ch.r: EBIT ÷ (working capital + net fixed assets) in the top 30%
ch.w: Every ₹100 tied up in plant and working capital earns ₹28 of operating profit.

ch.n: Near the top of the Magic Formula list
ch.r: Combined rank (earnings-yield rank + return rank) in the top 10%
ch.w: Greenblatt's method (STATED) buys the best 20–30 combined ranks; 'top 10%' is our cut-off.

lenses.sp: Nine quick tests of whether the business got healthier this year than last.
lenses.vd: In Piotroski F-score's spirit: would likely find a lot to like.

ch.r: Return on assets above zero
ch.w: Made a profit on its assets last year.

ch.r: Operating cash flow above zero
ch.w: The business brought in real cash.

ch.r: ROA higher than the year before
ch.w: Getting more profit out of its assets.

ch.r: Operating cash flow > net profit
ch.w: Profits backed by cash, not just accounting entries.

ch.r: Long-term debt ÷ assets lower than last year
ch.w: Less reliance on long-term loans.

ch.r: Current ratio higher than last year
ch.w: A thicker short-term cushion.

ch.r: Gross margin higher than last year
ch.w: Keeps more of each sale after direct costs.

ch.r: Share count not higher than last year
ch.w: Owners weren't diluted.

ch.r: Sales ÷ assets higher than last year
ch.w: Squeezing more sales out of what it owns.

lenses.st: Small, ambitious companies with big markets
lenses.sp: Looks for small companies run by experienced, ambitious people in huge markets – and patience.
lenses.vd: In Vijay Kedia's spirit: would likely find a lot to like.

ch.r: Market value under ₹5,000 crore

ch.r: Management with a proven record in this business

ch.r: Clear, ambitious growth plans

ch.r: Big, growing market to sell into

ch.r: Willing to hold for years

ch.r: No SEBI orders, auditor exits or similar red flags

ch.r: No management red flags in our automatic checks

Buy zone: below ₹194 (25% under the absolute value ₹259, 🛡️ Strict view), if the view's own conditions hold, confidence is Medium or High and the trend is up. Accumulate zone: ₹424–₹573 (consensus ₹498).
Moves to Trim above ₹648 (30% over fair value).

Any new serious red flag (auditor resigns mid-term, pledge above 25%, SEBI order, negative net worth, weak cash conversion together with high accruals, distress with interest cover below 1.5×) moves it straight to Avoid.
